title: Japonindolates A–C: new indole diterpenoids from the endophytic fungus  Aspergillus japonicus  334 and their anti-inflammatory activities
content: Chemical investigations on the endophytic fungus Aspergillus japonicus 334 yielded six structurally diverse indole diterpenoids (1–6) including three new compounds, namely japonindolates A–C (1–3). Their structures were elucidated by comprehensive spectroscopic analyses, including NMR, HRESIMS, electronic circular dichroism calculations, and quantum-chemical NMR calculations. The anti-inflammatory activities of compounds 1–6 were evaluated in lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-stimulated RAW264.7 macrophages and an LPS-induced inflammation model using Tg(mpx:EGFP) transgenic zebrafish larvae. In RAW264.7 macrophages, compounds 1–6 significantly reduced LPS-induced TNF-α secretion, compounds 2–4 and 6 decreased IL-1β secretion, and compounds 3–6 reduced NO production. In zebrafish larvae, compounds 2–4 and 6 significantly inhibited LPS-induced neutrophil recruitment, whereas compounds 1 and 5 showed no significant effects. Among the tested compounds, compound 4 showed the most pronounced activity across the tested inflammatory endpoints, followed by compound 6. These findings expand the chemical diversity of indole diterpenoids from endophytic fungi and highlight their potential as anti-inflammatory scaffolds for further investigation.
